title: Sample and Stand (2019)
headline: Theorem 2(a) is false as stated, and a step in Lemma B2 needs an assumption the paper does not state.

claims.label: Theorem 2(a)
claims.gist: Every entry game in the class has a symmetric pure equilibrium.
claims.statement: Every entry game satisfying Assumptions A1–A3 has a symmetric equilibrium in pure strategies.
claims.quantifiers: for every game satisfying the assumptions

result.summary: An entry game satisfying A1–A3 whose pure equilibria are all asymmetric.
result.witness: With three potential entrants and a market that is profitable for exactly two, every pure equilibrium has two entrants and one stays out, so none is symmetric.
result.tested: Games with two to four entrants and profit functions on a grid, solved exactly.
not_claimed: Part (b) of Theorem 2, on mixed equilibria, is not claimed to be false.
The theorem is not claimed to fail when entry is profitable for every number of entrants.
result.repair_note: Allowing mixed strategies restores the conclusion in all cases checked.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

checks.detail: A separate AI session, not given the earlier result, rebuilt the game.
The researcher solved the game exactly with separate code.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.novelty: No earlier report found in the searched literature.

claims.label: Lemma B2
claims.gist: The entry best-reply map has a closed graph.
claims.statement: The best-reply correspondence of the entry game has a closed graph in the space of entry probabilities.
claims.quantifiers: for every game satisfying the assumptions

result.summary: A closed graph needs profits to be continuous in the number of entrants; this is not stated.
result.witness: The limit step uses continuity of profits in the number of entrants; without it the graph is not closed in a three-entrant game with a profit jump.
result.tested: The proof read line by line; the three-entrant game used as a test case.
not_claimed: The lemma is not claimed to fail when profits are continuous in the number of entrants.
result.repair_note: Adding continuity of profits closes the step.
